draft.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu unifies Japan
card: For about a century, Japan's daimyo fought each other in long civil wars. The emperor had little real power to stop them.
Tokugawa Ieyasu was a powerful daimyo. In 1600 his army won the Battle of Sekigahara against rival daimyo.
In 1603 the emperor gave Ieyasu the title of shogun. He now led Japan as its military ruler.
The Tokugawa family kept the title of shogun for more than 250 years. This was a long period of peace.
draft.remember: Victory at Sekigahara in 1600 made Ieyasu shogun in 1603, and Tokugawa rule brought lasting peace.

a.q: What happened soon after Tokugawa Ieyasu won the Battle of Sekigahara?
opts: He became shogun and started Tokugawa rule
He gave up power and the emperor ruled alone
He was defeated and the civil wars went on
He became emperor and ended the shogun's role
a.why: Winning at Sekigahara left Ieyasu the strongest daimyo, and in 1603 he became shogun. The emperor did not take over, because the shogun was the military ruler and the emperor had little real power.
a.clue: Look at what title Ieyasu received in 1603.

b.q: Why did Tokugawa rule bring a long period of peace after years of civil war?
opts: One shogun now led Japan and his family held power
The emperor took back control from the daimyo
The daimyo agreed to fight only in other countries
Samurai were no longer allowed to serve daimyo
b.why: The civil wars happened because daimyo fought each other for power. After Sekigahara, Ieyasu became shogun and his family kept the title for over 250 years, so one ruler led Japan. The emperor still had little real power.
b.clue: Think about who held power after 1603.

a.best: He became shogun and started Tokugawa rule

b.best: One shogun now led Japan and his family held power
